title: Working Out the Points a Circle Redemption Spends
content:
## 1. What a redemption spends

The points a redemption spends on a Northbeam Circle Membership are the whole blocks of the balance a member
may release at once, and never more points than what they are being spent against is worth at the tier's value
per hundred points. Points are redeemed only while the membership stands active.

## 2. The balance a member may release

The balance a member may release starts from the live balance, which is the points earned over the whole ledger
less every point spent and every point swept. A live balance worked out on this schedule never falls below
nothing.

Only a share of that live balance may be released in one redemption. The whole of the live balance may be
released.

## 3. Points held back against what the member owes

Points are then held back against money the member already owes Northbeam on other lines, each amount held back
being taken at the tier's value per hundred points. The figure left when the amounts held back are taken off the
share released never falls below nothing: where those amounts come to more than that share, no points stand to
be released. No points are held back for goods coming back. No points are held back for cover. No points are
held back for work.

## 4. What the redemption is being spent against

What the redemption is being spent against is what stands unsettled on the profile's orders, taken as the
charges billed less the credits applied and the payments taken over the twelve months ending on the handling
day, and the points that amount is worth are it taken at the tier's value per hundred points. Where the credits
applied and the payments taken come to as much as the charges billed or more, nothing stands unsettled on those
orders.

A redemption put against a charge already standing on the profile is taken as an instant discount on that
charge rather than as a certificate the member spends later.

## 5. The order the figure is settled in

The order is fixed: the live balance is settled first, the share released is applied to it, the three amounts
held back are then taken off one after another, the figure is capped at what the redemption is being spent
against is worth, and only then is it brought down to whole blocks of the tier's minimum redemption block; a
balance below one block cannot be redeemed at all.

## 6. The figure worked through on hypothetical entries

Take a membership on Circle Business Elite, whose value per hundred points is 1.25 and whose minimum
redemption block is 100 points, with a ledger carrying 46300 points earned over the whole of it, 8150 points
spent and 3200 points swept: the live balance is 34950 points. Take for this illustration the whole of the live
balance as the share released and nothing held back for goods coming back, for cover or for work, so 34950
points stand releasable.

Take the profile's orders as carrying 1480.00 of charges billed, 185.00 of credits applied and 760.00 of
payments taken over the twelve months ending on the handling day: 535.00 stands unsettled, which at 1.25 per
hundred points is worth 42800 points. The figure is capped at 42800 and so stays at 34950, and 34950 brought
down to whole blocks of 100 points is 34900 points.

Had the orders carried 980.00 of payments instead, 315.00 would stand unsettled, worth 25200 points at the
same rate; the figure would then be capped at 25200 points, which is already a whole number of blocks.
